question: A previously healthy 57-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of acute retrosternal chest pain that radiates to his back. The pain started suddenly while he was having dinner. A few moments prior to the onset of the pain, he experienced discomfort when trying to eat or drink anything. On the way to the hospital he took a sublingual nitrate tablet that he had at home, which helped relieve the pain. His pulse is 80/min, respirations are 14/min, and blood pressure is 144/88 mm Hg. Examination shows no other abnormalities. An ECG shows a normal sinus rhythm with no ST-segment abnormalities. An esophagogram is done and shows areas of diffuse, uncoordinated spasms in several segments along the length of the esophagus. This patient's condition is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.opa: Esophageal manometry shows simultaneous multi-peak contractions
options.opc: Ultrasonography shows a mass at the gastroesophageal junction

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Diffuse, uncoordinated spasms in several segments of the esophagus -> Possible esophageal motility disorder -> Possible esophageal dysmotility -> 70%
enhanced_information: The patient's condition of diffuse, uncoordinated esophageal spasms is most likely indicative of esophageal motility disorder. Esophageal manometry showing simultaneous multi-peak contractions is a common finding in this condition, supporting option A (Esophageal manometry shows simultaneous multi-peak contractions). Endoscopy showing multiple mucosal erosions or ultrasonography showing a mass at the gastroesophageal junction are less likely in this context. Serology showing elevated CK-MB levels is not typically associated with esophageal motility disorders.
analysis: The patient's presentation of acute retrosternal chest pain with radiation to the back, associated with difficulty eating or drinking and relieved by sublingual nitrate, along with esophageal spasms on esophagogram, is highly suggestive of esophageal motility disorder. The most common finding in this condition is simultaneous multi-peak contractions on esophageal manometry, supporting option A.
